Luis Walter Alvarez is a physicist. Alvarez devised a set of experiments to observe K-electron capture in radioactive nuclei, predicted by the beta decay theory but never before observed.
Pick the chemist from these four.
What is the atomic number of Lithium?
Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.
In what year was Pope Benedict XVI born?
Pope Benedict XVI: Following his resignation, he chose to be known as "pope emeritus", a title he held until his death on 31 December 2022.
In what year was Iodine discovered?
Iodine is a chemical element; it has symbol I and atomic number 53.
In what year was Nickel discovered?
Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
Magnesium sulfate: Pfizer. It is a white crystalline solid, soluble in water.
In which country is Blood orange?
Blood orange: Italy. The blood orange is a variety of orange with crimson, near blood-colored flesh.
Who is credited with discovering Caesium?
Caesium: Robert Bunsen. Caesium (IUPAC spelling; also spelled cesium in American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
Who is credited with discovering Nobelium?
Nobelium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Nobelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol No and atomic number 102.
Who is credited with discovering Silicon?
Silicon: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.

Sometimes called a nerve impulse or 'spike,' this rapid rise and fall of voltage across a cell membrane ripples to neighboring spots and fires in neurons, muscle cells, and even some plant cells. What is it?
Action potential (also known as a nerve impulse or "spike" when in a neuron) is a series of quick changes in voltage across a cell membrane.

With roughly 370 million individuals, this migratory thrush outnumbers red-winged blackbirds and starlings across its home continent, despite being misnamed after an unrelated European species — what is it?
American robin (Turdus migratorius) is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family.
This Portuguese economist-turned-dictator ruled as head of government from 1932 to 1968, rebranding his authoritarian regime as the corporatist 'New State.' Who is he?
António de Oliveira Salazar (28 April 1889 - 27 July 1970) was a Portuguese dictator, academic, and economist who served as President of the Council of Ministers of Portugal from 1932 to 1968.
This American psychologist developed the philosophy of radical behaviorism and pioneered operant conditioning while a longtime professor at Harvard — who is he?
B. F. Skinner (March 20, 1904 - August 18, 1990) was an American psychologist, behaviorist, inventor, and social philosopher.

First flickering to life in octocorals some 540 million years ago and evolving independently at least 94 separate times, this glow is sometimes borrowed from symbiotic bacteria — what is the phenomenon?
Bioluminescence is the production of light by an organism as the result of a chemiluminescence reaction.

David Attenborough called this English particle physicist the natural successor for the BBC's scientific programming, thanks to shows like The Infinite Monkey Cage and his Wonders of... series — who is he?
Brian Cox (physicist) (born 3 March 1968) is an English physicist and musician.
Nine to ten times as massive as the Sun and expanded to 71 times its radius, this blue-loop giant in the constellation Carina ranks second only to Sirius in night-sky brightness — which star?
Canopus is the brightest star in the southern constellation of Carina and the second-brightest star in the night sky.
Domesticated from the red junglefowl of Southeast Asia about 8,000 years ago, this social bird now numbers over 26.5 billion worldwide — what is it?
Chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus) is the domesticated form of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), originally native to Southeast Asia.

Lacking the sucking mouthparts of aphids, this chewing-mouthed insect is considered one of the most primitive alive — and a famous few of its 4,600 species became notorious household pests. What is it?
Cockroach (or roaches) are insects belonging to the order Blattodea (Blattaria).
This is the capacity to produce novel, valuable ideas or works — whether an invention, a scientific theory, a joke, or a piece of jewelry — through the exercise of imagination — what's the capacity?
Creativity is the ability to generate novel and valuable ideas or works through the exercise of imagination.

Named from the Latin word for 'finger' because of its tubular, spike-borne flowers, this genus of about 20 European and West Asian species was reclassified into a new plant family in 2001 — what is it commonly called?
Digitalis (or) is a genus of about 20 species of herbaceous perennial plants, shrubs, and biennials, commonly called foxgloves.
Sometimes occurring spontaneously during sleep as a nocturnal emission, this process involves the discharge of semen through the urethra — what is it called?
Ejaculation is the discharge of semen (the ejaculate; normally containing sperm) from the penis through the urethra.

This simple hydrocarbon gas, the simplest member of a class called alkenes, is the most-produced organic compound on Earth by tonnage, and is the primary building block of a common plastic — what is it?
Ethylene (IUPAC name: ethene) is a hydrocarbon which has the formula C2H4 or H2C=CH2.
Encompassing everything from oral tales and proverbs to festival rituals and traditional building styles, what term describes the shared expressive culture of a group?
Folklore is the body of expressive culture shared by a particular group of people, culture or subculture.
The largest of four living anteater species, this terrestrial mammal of Central and South America is known for its elongated snout, bushy tail, and long foreclaws. What is it?
Giant anteater (Myrmecophaga tridactyla) is an insectivorous mammal native to Central and South America.
What protein filament, grown from follicles in the skin's dermis layer and composed mainly of alpha-keratin, is one of the defining characteristics of mammals?
Hair is a protein filament that grows from follicles found in the dermis.

Known taxonomically as Lonicera, this genus of 158 species of arching shrubs and twining vines is native to northern latitudes worldwide, though one of its Asian members has become a notorious invasive pest — what's the plant?
Honeysuckle are arching shrubs or twining vines in the genus Lonicera of the family Caprifoliaceae.
Supplied by the lumbar spinal nerves and part of the femoral nerve, this fused pair of abdominal and thigh muscles is the body's strongest hip flexor — what is it called?
Iliopsoas (from Latin ile 'groin' and Ancient Greek (ps) 'muscles of the loins') refers to the joined psoas major and the iliacus muscles.
This French mathematician of algebraic topology and number theory pulled off a rare double: the Fields Medal in 1954 and, nearly fifty years later, the very first Abel Prize. Who was he?
Jean-Pierre Serre (born 15 September 1926) is a French mathematician who has made contributions to algebraic topology, algebraic geometry and algebraic number theory.
Native to eastern and southern Africa, this flowering shrub is the sole species in its genus and has a documented history of cultivation dating back to Ethiopia's Harar region. Name the plant?
Khat (Catha edulis), also known as Bushman's tea, especially in South Africa, is a species of flowering plant in the family Celastraceae, and the sole species in genus Catha.

This group of blood cancers typically begins in the bone marrow and produces abnormal blood cells called blasts. Symptoms include bleeding, bruising, bone pain, and fever due to a lack of normal blood cells — what is this disease?
Leukemia (also spelled leukaemia) is a group of blood cancers that usually begin in the bone marrow and produce high numbers of abnormal blood cells.
Its name is Latin for 'wolf,' and this autoimmune disease cycles between flares and remission, often announcing itself with a red rash across the face — what is it?
Lupus (SLE), is an autoimmune disease in which the body's immune system mistakenly attacks healthy tissue in many parts of the body.
Number theory, algebra, geometry, analysis and set theory are all branches of this field, which leans on logical reasoning and proof to study abstract concepts — what is it?
Mathematics is a field of knowledge concerned with abstract concepts such as numbers, geometric shapes, sets, functions, and probabilities.
First flown by the Soviet Air Force in 1968 and still in Russian production today, this medium chopper carries the NATO reporting name 'Hip' — what aircraft is it?
Mil Mi-8 is a family of medium twin-turbine helicopters, originally designed by the Soviet Central Aerohydrodynamic Institute (TsAGI) in the 1960s and introduced into the Soviet Air Force in 1968.
Unlike its cousin hemoglobin, this protein binds oxygen without cooperative binding and only shows up in a human's bloodstream after muscle injury — which protein?
Myoglobin (symbol Mb or MB) is an iron- and oxygen-binding protein found in the cardiac and skeletal muscle tissue of vertebrates in general and in almost all mammals.
The smallest of its type, this Canadian gun dog has webbed feet and lures waterfowl to shore with playful antics before fetching them from the water — which breed is it?
Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever is a medium-sized gun dog bred primarily for hunting.

Created by Danish-Canadian programmer Rasmus Lerdorf in 1993 and released in 1995, this general-purpose scripting language was originally short for 'Personal Home Page' before becoming a recursive backronym — name the language?
PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
This class of compounds is defined by a direct single bond between two oxygen atoms, denoted R−O−O−R — what are they called?
Peroxide are a group of molecules with the structure ROOR, where each R represents a radical (a portion of a complete molecule; not a free radical) and the O's are single oxygen atoms.
Its common name is shared with an unrelated tropical fruit, but this genus of roughly 200 herbaceous species — also called fleaworts — belongs to the family Plantaginaceae. Which genus?
Plantago is a genus of about 200 species of flowering plants in the family Plantaginaceae, commonly called plantains or fleaworts.

Derived enzymatically from a fatty acid found in nearly every tissue of the body, this class of lipid compounds produces diverse hormone-like effects despite not being true hormones — what are they called?
Prostaglandin (PG) are a group of physiologically active lipid compounds that have diverse hormone-like effects in animals.
Along with his two brothers, this American physician-turned-businessman acquired the pharmaceutical company behind OxyContin, later linked to the U.S. opioid crisis — who is he?
Raymond Sackler (February 16, 1920 - July 17, 2017) was an American physician and businessman.

Named after the naturalist who first documented it, this highly venomous South Asian snake is known for an extremely painful bite and ranks among the region's 'Big Four' dangerous species — what snake is it?
Russell's viper (Daboia russelii) is a species of highly venomous snake in the family Viperidae.

Native only to groves on California's Sierra Nevada slopes, this conifer species includes the largest trees on Earth by volume, though fewer than 80,000 remain and it's now listed as endangered — what's the species?

Sequoiadendron giganteum (also known as the giant sequoia, giant redwood, Sierra redwood or Wellingtonia) is a species of coniferous tree, classified in the family Cupressaceae in the subfamily Sequoioideae.
This Polish-American Gestalt psychologist insisted 'most social acts lose meaning if isolated' — a credo that shaped his famous experiments on conformity and impression formation. Who was he?
Solomon Asch (September 14, 1907 - February 20, 1996) was a Polish-American Gestalt psychologist and pioneer in social psychology.
This small nocturnal marsupial sails between trees on membranes stretched from wrist to ankle, and its Latin name translates as 'short-headed rope-dancer' — what animal is it?
Sugar glider (Petaurus breviceps) is a small, omnivorous, arboreal, and nocturnal gliding possum.
This vast domain of human practice — divided into visual, literary, and performing branches — lets people transmit values, ideas, and experiences across generations. What is it?
The arts are a vast range of human practices involving creative expression, storytelling, and cultural participation.
Caused by a single-celled parasite and often symptom-free, this common STI can be diagnosed by examining vaginal fluid under a microscope or with a DNA test — what is it?
Trichomoniasis (trich) is an infectious disease caused by the parasite Trichomonas vaginalis.
This broad category of creative disciplines spans painting, sculpture, photography, and architecture, and includes applied fields like industrial and fashion design — what do we call it?
Visual arts are art forms such as painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, photography, video, image, filmmaking, design, crafts, and architecture.
This Russian political activist and economist, described as the 'first lady' of her country's opposition, vowed to continue her late husband's work after fleeing into exile. Who is she?
Yulia Navalnaya (ne Abrosimova; born 24 July 1976) is a Russian political activist and economist.
This protrusion in the neck, formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage around the larynx, becomes more prominent in most men during puberty — what is it?
Adam's apple: Feature of the neck. The Adam's apple is the protrusion in the neck formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage surrounding the larynx, typically visible in men and less so in women.

This organic functional group, structured R−CH=O and alternatively called a formyl group when isolated from its side chain, appears throughout biologically and technologically important chemicals — what is it?
Aldehyde: Organic compound containing the functional group R–CH=O.
Sold under the brand name Norvasc, this long-acting calcium channel blocker treats high blood pressure and variant angina by relaxing and widening the arteries — what's the drug?
Amlodipine: Medication against high blood pressure.
Caused by the bacterium Bacillus anthracis, its skin form starts as a small blister that becomes a painless ulcer with a telltale black center — what infection is this?
Anthrax: Infection caused by Bacillus anthracis bacteria. The skin form presents with a small blister with surrounding swelling that often turns into a painless ulcer with a black center.
Literally meaning "hardening of the arteries," this umbrella term covers vascular disorders marked by abnormal thickening and loss of elasticity in artery walls — what is it called?
Arteriosclerosis: Thickening, hardening and loss of elasticity of the walls of arteries.
Sold as Zithromax, this antibiotic tackles strep throat, pneumonia and traveler's diarrhea — but its tendency to cause QT prolongation keeps doctors watchful of the heart. Which drug is it?
Azithromycin: Antibiotic. It is administered by mouth, into a vein, or as topical treatment for the eye.
Built atop an Ilyushin transport and nicknamed 'Mainstay,' this Soviet radar plane had its existence leaked to the West by a spy in 1978 — which aircraft is it?
Beriev A-50: Soviet airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft.
Originally launched as the McDonnell Douglas MD-95, this narrow-body airliner seats up to 134 passengers with twin engines mounted at the tail — which jet?
Ranging from roughly seawater-strength up to a fully saturated 26%, which salty solution is used for pickling food, de-icing roads, and turns up as a wastewater byproduct of desalination?
Brine: Concentrated solution of salt in water.
Named for the Latin word for the first day of the month, this daisy-family genus is commonly called marigold and is prized in herbal and cosmetic products — which plant?
Calendula: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae.
Its Greek-derived genus name Xylocopa literally means 'wood-cutter,' fitting for an insect that burrows nesting tunnels into dead wood or bamboo — which insect is it?
Carpenter bee: Common name for a genus of bees.
Also known as silver beet or perpetual spinach, this leafy green shares its species with beetroot — which vegetable?
Chard: Green leafy vegetable. Chard (Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris, Cicla Group and Flavescens Group) is a green leafy vegetable.
Sold under the brand name Celexa, this SSRI antidepressant treats major depressive disorder, OCD, panic disorder, and social anxiety — what is it?
Citalopram: SSRI antidepressant. Citalopram, sold under the brand name Celexa among others, is an antidepressant of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class.
In mathematics, this is a selection of items from a set where the order of choosing them does not matter, unlike a permutation — what is it called?

Combination: Selection of items from a set. In mathematics, a combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations).
Domesticated in Africa and thriving in sandy, low-rainfall soil, this ancient legume is now grown mostly in Nigeria and Niger, which together supply two-thirds of the world's crop — which plant?
Cowpea: Species of plant. The cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) is an annual herbaceous legume from the genus Vigna.
Son of a bass-baritone and born into a family of engineers, this American built his first car at 19, won four F1 Grands Prix, and took Le Mans in 1967 — who was he?
Dan Gurney: American racing driver, engineer and motorsport executive (1931–2018)
Nicknamed 'dumb cane' because its poisonous sap can temporarily rob you of speech, this shade-tolerant tropical houseplant is native to the New World — which genus?
Dieffenbachia: Genus of plants. Dieffenbachia, commonly known as dumb cane or leopard lily, is a genus of tropical flowering plants in the family Araceae.
This plant genus in the mallow family produces the world's most famously pungent fruit, alongside eight other edible-fruit-bearing species — which genus?
Durio: Genus of plants. Several species produce an edible fruit known as durian, the most common species being Durio zibethinus, with eight others producing edible fruit.

The heaviest aircraft ever built by its Brazilian manufacturer, this twin-engine jet transport was developed as a derivative of a regional jetliner, similar in role to the C-130 Hercules. Which aircraft?
Embraer C-390 Millennium: Brazilian military transport aircraft/tanker.
The simplest alkene and the most-produced organic compound on Earth, this colorless gas is also a natural plant hormone used to ripen fruit — what is it?
This principle describes how a changing magnetic field generates an electric current, underpinning the operation of transformers, generators, and motors — what is it called?
Faraday's law of induction: Basic law of electromagnetism.
The lightest halogen, this pale yellow gas is so reactive that several 19th-century chemists died or were injured trying to isolate it, until Henri Moissan finally succeeded in 1886 — which element?
Fluorine: Chemical element with atomic number 9 (F)
Tucked beneath the liver, this pear-shaped organ stores and concentrates bile before releasing it to aid fat digestion in the small intestine — which organ?
Gallbladder: Organ in humans and other vertebrates.
The tallest land animal alive and the largest ruminant on Earth, its closest living relative is the okapi — which long-necked African mammal is it?
Unlike its rocky, mountain-dwelling marmot relatives, this solitary lowland rodent — also called the woodchuck — is common across the Eastern U.S., Canada, and Alaska. What is it?
Groundhog: Species of rodent. The groundhog (Marmota monax), also known as the woodchuck, is a rodent of the family Sciuridae, belonging to the group of large ground squirrels known as marmots.
This wingless insect spends its entire life on the human scalp, sipping blood, and can neither fly nor jump — its short stumpy legs can't even walk well on a flat surface. What tiny freeloader is it?
Head louse: Insect parasite of humans.
Also called urticaria, this skin condition brings red or flesh-colored raised, itchy bumps that may sting and often follow an allergic reaction — what is it?
Hives: Skin disease characterized by red, raised, and itchy bumps.
Named from Greek words meaning "over" and "formation," this condition enlarges tissue by increasing the number of cells rather than their size — which term, distinct from hypertrophy?
Hyperplasia: Enlargement of tissue due to cell proliferation.
Commonly known as chaga, this parasitic fungus grows on birch trees and forms a charcoal-like black mass often marketed, questionably, as a health supplement — what's its scientific name?
Inonotus obliquus: Species of fungus. Inonotus obliquus, commonly called chaga (a Latinization of the Russian word ча́га), is a fungus in the family Hymenochaetaceae.
The first woman to chair the Federal Reserve, this American economist later became the first woman to serve as U.S. Treasury secretary — who is she?
Janet Yellen: American economist and government official (born 1946)
Also known as the English or Persian walnut, this tree species native to Eurasia is cultivated worldwide, with China as its leading producer today — what is it?
Juglans regia: Species of tree (walnut). Juglans regia, known by various common names including the common walnut, English walnut, or Persian walnut amongst other names, is a species of walnut.

Ranked alongside Aristotle and Frege among history's most significant logicians, this thinker proved his completeness theorem in his 1929 Vienna dissertation before publishing his famous incompleteness theorems two years later — who is he?
Kurt Gödel: Mathematical logician and philosopher.
Often called the last physicist to master every branch of the field, this Soviet scientist co-discovered the density matrix method and developed the theory of superfluidity — who is he?
Marketed as Imodium, this opioid-class medication treats diarrhea without crossing the blood-brain barrier at normal doses?
Loperamide: Medicine used to reduce diarrhea.
Transmitted through the bite of infected Anopheles mosquitoes and caused by single-celled Plasmodium parasites, which disease's symptoms typically begin 10 to 15 days after infection?
Powered by two rear-mounted engines under a T-tail and fitted with built-in airstairs, this twin-engine jetliner entered service with Delta Air Lines in December 1965 — which aircraft is it?
McDonnell Douglas DC-9: Jet airliner, produced 1965-1982.
Used to treat nausea, vomiting, and gastroparesis, this dopamine receptor antagonist is also prescribed for migraines and appears on the WHO's List of Essential Medicines — what is it?
Metoclopramide: Medication. It is thus rarely recommended that people take the medication for longer than twelve weeks.
Its dust-like, colored, fuzzy appearance on food comes from spores, and its branching network of hyphae — called a mycelium — counts as a single organism; what fungal structure is this?
Mold: Wooly, dust-like fungal structure or substance.
Lacking a cell wall entirely, this genus of bacteria is naturally resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics that target cell-wall synthesis — which genus?
Mycoplasma: Genus of bacteria. Mycoplasma is a genus of bacteria that, like the other members of the class Mollicutes, lack a cell wall (peptidoglycan) around their cell membrane.
This semiaquatic salamander's juvenile phase is nicknamed an 'eft,' and adults return to the water every year to breed after living mostly on land — what is it?
Newt: Salamander in the subfamily Pleurodelinae.
Weighing up to 1,000 kg and resembling a fish head without a tail, this giant marine creature can be as tall as it is long when its fins are extended — what is it?
Ocean sunfish: Species of fish. The ocean sunfish (Mola mola), also known as the common mola, is one of the largest bony fish in the world.
This genus of highly sociable ruminants includes domestic sheep, believed to descend from the wild mouflon of central and southwest Asia — which genus?
Ovis: Genus of mammals. Ovis is a genus of mammals, part of the Caprinae subfamily of the ruminant family Bovidae.
This economist and longtime New York Times columnist was the sole winner of the 2008 Nobel for his work on new trade theory and economic geography. Who is he?
Sold under brand names like Sudafed PE, this nasal decongestant works as a selective alpha-1 adrenergic receptor agonist — what is the drug?
Phenylephrine: Decongestant medication. It is unclear whether its use during pregnancy and breastfeeding is safe.
This egg-laying Australian mammal hunts with its eyes, ears, and nostrils shut, sensing prey by electrolocation — and, oddly for a mammal, it's also venomous. What is it?
Platypus: Species of mammal. Like other monotremes, the platypus has a sense of electrolocation, which it uses to detect prey in water while its eyes, ears and nostrils are closed.
This legal document spells out how a business collects, stores, and shares personal details like your address, financial records, or medical history — what is it called?
Privacy policy: Management of personal data across media.
Recognizable by its bold red-and-black pattern, this true bug is often confused with the unrelated cinnamon bug and forms large aggregations across Europe and Asia — which species is it?
Pyrrhocoris apterus: Species of true bug. The firebug, Pyrrhocoris apterus, is a common insect of the family Pyrrhocoridae.
Scholars call it an "essentially contested concept" with no agreed definition, but it broadly links humanity to the supernatural through behaviors, ethics, texts and sacred places — what is it?
This enormous flowering-plant family, named for its type genus, gives us apples, cherries, strawberries, and ornamental roses alike — which plant family is it?
Rosaceae: Rose family of flowering plants.
A former finance minister and central bank board member, this economist became the 52nd president of Paraguay in 2023 after switching from a liberal party to the Colorado Party — who is he?
Santiago Peña: President of Paraguay since 2023. Peña served on leadership boards for the Central Bank of Paraguay and Banco Amambay.
Considered paradoxical by the ancient Greeks in Zeno's puzzle about motion, what term describes an infinite sum of terms added one after another, later made rigorous through the concept of a limit?
Series (mathematics): Infinite sum. In mathematics, a series is, roughly speaking, an addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.
The sixth most abundant element in Earth's crust, this soft alkali metal carries symbol Na and pairs with chlorine as the ocean's most common dissolved element — what is it?
Sodium: Chemical element with atomic number 11 (Na)

Developed in 1962 by an American pharmaceutical company and derived from a natural male hormone, this anabolic steroid treats hereditary angioedema and is unusual for surviving liver metabolism without being esterified — what is it?
Stanozolol: Discontinued steroid for heart treatment.

Blending geodesy, trigonometry, and law, this profession uses tools like theodolites, GNSS receivers, and lidar scanners to fix the exact positions of points on Earth for maps and property boundaries — what is it?
Surveying: Science of determining the positions of points and the distances and angles between them.

Named after the Latin word for 'earth' despite being one of the rarest elements in Earth's crust, this brittle silver-white metalloid with atomic number 52 was first found in a Transylvanian gold mine — what is it?
Tellurium: Chemical element with atomic number 52 (Te)

Spread by the bite of certain infected arachnids, this viral illness of the central nervous system can cause meningitis and lasting cognitive problems, with cases up nearly 400% across Europe in three decades — what is it?

Tick-borne encephalitis: Viral infection of the nervous system. Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) is a viral infectious disease involving the central nervous system, transmitted by the bite of several species of infected ticks.
This chromosomal condition gives a female an extra sex chromosome beyond the usual pair, often producing no noticeable symptoms — fewer than 1 in 10 who have it even know. What is the condition?
Trisomy X: Chromosome disorder in women.
This Soviet chemist led efforts to contain the 1986 Chernobyl disaster and later briefed the international community in Vienna, though he omitted key design flaws in the reactor. Who was he?
Valery Legasov: Former Soviet inorganic chemist and member of the USSR Academy of Sciences (1936–1988)
In quantum mechanics, this idea captures how photons and electrons can act like discrete billiard-ball-like objects in some experiments and like spreading ripples in others — what is it?
Wave–particle duality: Concept in quantum mechanics. It expresses the inability of the classical concepts such as particle or wave to fully describe the behavior of quantum objects.
Spread mainly by the oriental rat flea, this gram-negative bacterium caused the Black Death and the Plague of Justinian — what is it?
Yersinia pestis: Species of bacteria, cause of plague.
The symbol for caesium is Cs. Caesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
The symbol for livermorium is Lv. Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.

In what year was Gérard Depardieu born?
Gérard Depardieu: Gérard Xavier Marcel Depardieu (UK:, US:, French: [ʒeʁaʁ ɡzavje maʁsɛl dəpaʁdjø]; born 27 December 1948) is a French actor.
In what year was Priyanka Chopra born?
Priyanka Chopra Jonas (née Chopra; born 18 July 1982) is an Indian actress and film producer.
In what year was Katie Holmes born?
Katie Holmes (born Kate Noelle Holmes; December 18, 1978) is an American actress and filmmaker.
In what year was Jensen Ackles born?
Jensen Ackles: Jensen Ross Ackles (born March 1, 1978) is an American actor and musician.
In what year was Emma Roberts born?
Emma Roberts: Emma Rose Roberts (born February 10, 1991) is an American actress, singer, and producer.
In what year was Kelly Preston born?
Kelly Preston: Kelly Kamalelehua Smith (October 13, 1962 – July 12, 2020), known professionally as Kelly Preston, was an American actress.
In what year was Freddie Highmore born?
Freddie Highmore: Alfred Thomas Highmore (born 14 February 1992) is an English actor.

Emmy Rossum: Emmanuelle Grey Rossum (born September 12, 1986) is an American actress and singer.
In what year was Alicia Vikander born?
Alicia Vikander: Alicia Amanda Vikander (Swedish: [aˈlǐːsɪa vɪˈkǎnːdɛr]; born 3 October 1988) is a Swedish actress.
In what year was Elizabeth Debicki born?
Elizabeth Debicki (born 24 August 1990) is an Australian actress.
In what year was Lee Min-ho born?
Lee Min-ho (Korean: 이민호, born June 22, 1987) is a South Korean actor and singer.
In what year did Natalie Wood die?
Natalie Wood (née Zacharenko; July 20, 1938 – November 29, 1981) was an American actress.
In what year did Jimmy Savile die?
